title: Grace acts beyond illumination and invitation
source_text: XXXI. Si quaeratur, An praeter mentis illustrationem, & affectuum excitationem, & voluntatis invitationem nihil faciat Gratia per modum principii, vel antecedenter ad conversionem? Respondemus facere. Quod autem gratia praeterea facit, videtur, ex eorum mente, esse novarum illarum virium infusio, de qua antea locuti sunt.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. If it is asked, Whether besides the illustration of the mind, & the excitation of the affections, & the invitation of the will Grace does nothing by way of principle, or antecedently to conversion? We answer that it does. But what grace does besides, seems, in their mind, to be the infusion of those new strengths, of which they spoke before.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXI. 'If it is asked whether, beyond enlightening the mind, stirring the affections and inviting the will, grace does nothing by way of principle or in advance of conversion, we answer that it does something.'
What grace does besides this seems, on their view, to be the infusion of the new strength they spoke of earlier.

lemmas.latin: per modum principii, vel antecedenter ad conversionem
lemmas.gloss: by way of principle, or antecedently to conversion
to be the infusion of those new strengths

choices.why: The Remonstrant term: grace acts so that the will can either yield to it or block it.
